title: Psalm 61: Lead Me to the Rock Higher Than I
summary: From the ends of the earth, with a fainting heart, the psalmist asks God to hear him and lead him to a rock too high for him to climb alone. He longs to live in God's tent and shelter under his wings, prays for the king's long life, and promises to praise God and keep his vows every day.

from.where: The Study Bible's notes on Psalm 64
from.text: Psalm 64 closes the small group of Davidic trust psalms in 61 to 64 and is the last lament before the three great songs of praise in Psalms 65 to 67.

line: From the ends of the earth, with a fainting heart, the psalmist asks to be led to a rock higher than he can climb, and longs to shelter in God's tent.
guide: When your heart is faint you cannot lift yourself; you need something firmer than you are, and someone to lead you to it. Pray verse 2 from wherever the ends of the earth are for you, and let verse 8 show the answer: faithfulness day by day, not all at once.

stanzas.title: A cry from the ends of the earth
Refuge in God's tent and under his wings
God has heard the vows and given an inheritance
A prayer for the king's long life
Praise and vows fulfilled day by day

verses.t: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. Of David. Hear my cry, O God; attend to my prayer.
From the ends of the earth I call out to You whenever my heart is faint. Lead me to the rock that is higher than I.
For You have been my refuge, a tower of strength against the enemy.
Let me dwell in Your tent forever and take refuge in the shelter of Your wings. Selah
For You have heard my vows, O God; You have given me the inheritance reserved for those who fear Your name.
Increase the days of the king’s life; may his years span many generations.
May he sit enthroned in God’s presence forever; appoint Your loving devotion and Your faithfulness to guard him.
Then I will ever sing praise to Your name and fulfill my vows day by day.
